# Wuffs (Wrangling Untrusted File Formats Safely)

- **Upstream:** https://github.com/google/wuffs
- **Version:** tag `v0.4.0-alpha.12`, commit `7f70dda95c77b10c087c0908790837b5e9c15713` (2026-10-20). The file reports `WUFFS_VERSION_STRING "0.4.0-alpha.12+4048.20261020"`.
  - **Why an alpha:** the 0.3 line is upstream's latest stable release, but it has no JPEG decoder. glTF textures are PNG or JPEG ([ADR 0036](../../docs/adr/0036-image-decoding.md)).
  - **What it means:** upstream promises no API stability for 0.4 alphas. Lykoware pins this exact file and wraps it, so an upstream change cannot reach the engine without a deliberate update.
- **Included:**
  - `release/c/wuffs-v0.4.c` as `wuffs-v0.4.c` (the whole single-file library, unmodified), SHA-256 `458066457347bd6d9bc3c906aa8292bea4488577727569ddd9436fdd89d5f04d`;
  - the upstream `LICENSE`, `LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE`, unchanged.
- **Licence:** upstream offers MIT or Apache-2.0; Lykoware uses it under MIT. Copyright 2023 The Wuffs Authors. Keep the notice in `LICENSE-MIT` with any distribution.
- **Local patches:** none.
- **Transitive dependencies:** none. The library uses only the C/C++ standard libraries. The C code is generated by upstream from Wuffs-the-language, which checks memory safety at compile time; the generated code needs no runtime checks for buffer overflows.
- **Built:**
  - one translation unit, `engine/src/image/wuffs_impl.cpp`, as the static target `lykoware_wuffs` (`cmake/VendorWuffs.cmake`), without Lykoware's warning flags or clang-tidy;
  - only the modules Lykoware uses are compiled: base, the C++ image helpers (`AUX__BASE`, `AUX__IMAGE`), PNG and its checksums and zlib decompression (`PNG`, `ZLIB`, `DEFLATE`, `ADLER32`, `CRC32`), and `JPEG`. Every other format is preprocessed out.
- **Wrapper:** `lykoware/image_decode.hpp` (`lykoware::decode_image`). No Wuffs type appears in a public header.
- **Updates:**
  - pin a new tag and record its commit and hash;
  - check the licence files;
  - replace the file;
  - run `assets.image` and a fuzz run of `decode_image` under ASan/UBSan, as ADR 0036 records.
